title: Cold outreach without a prospect database
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: How the owner builds a lawful account list by hand, finds the right contact, structures messages and books first meetings.
applies_when: Owner has hours to research and send from their own mailbox
exclusions: No lawful basis for contact in the jurisdiction
Owner hours below the playbook minimum
required_inputs: ICP traits tagged observable or not
evidence_requirements: 2-4 must-have traits marked observable or not observable
magnitude signals (how much pain or spend)
one primary public source that reliably shows the gating trait
team or about page naming roles
how the email was obtained (published verbatim, role address, owner import)
average deal value and meeting-to-win rate (owner estimate)
missing_data_behavior: Traits not observable: become discovery questions, not list filters.
No reply data: first campaign is step 1 plus one follow-up.

decision_branches.then: Step 1 plus one follow-up; up to 4 steps only after the owner reviews about 100 contacts.

decision_branches.if: Owner has warm connections at target accounts

decision_branches.then: Book with a lead time of about a week; invite and reminder hygiene.

implementation_steps: Write the minimum viable criteria (2-4) and why each predicts fit
List magnitude signals and a simple labelled attractiveness order
Pick account-first or contact-first by the cheapest gating trait
Pick one primary public source; use others only to enrich
Start in the owner's area when in-person meetings help
Collect 50-100 accounts by hand with source URLs and dates
Find titles on the company's own pages
Choose primary and one fallback contact
Get the route: published business email (verbatim), role address under the rules, form or phone
Map narrative themes to steps (1: core outcome, 2: new angle, 3: resource, 4: close-out)
Write follow-ups that each add something new
Send the calendar invite with location in both fields, a short agenda and a clear title
dependencies: prospect passed K3/K4 and jurisdiction checks
owner approval of template and sample messages

cash_and_labor_requirements.cash: None to small (registry or directory access)
cash_and_labor_requirements.labor: About 10-20 minutes per account by hand (our estimate, not the book's)
cash_and_labor_requirements.measurement: Share of listed accounts that turn out qualified in conversations

guardrails: Owner's mailbox only, never Resend; no bought or scraped lists without lawful basis; no pattern-guessed addresses.
No 'Re:' on first subjects, no links in step 1, no fake voicemails, no open-tracking triggers.
Public business sources only; no bought or scraped lists without a lawful basis
No personal addresses, LinkedIn scraping or email-finder tools that scrape profiles
Owner's own mailbox only, never Resend
No false urgency or invented slots
alternatives_when_constrained: Market too thin publicly: inbound capture (K8) or partners (PB-partners)
Gating trait not observable at all: lead magnet or content that makes buyers raise their hands (PB-lead-magnet)
No usable route: warm intro (K7), partner (PB-partners), or inbound (K8)
No mailbox: warm intros (K7) or partners
No owner availability: recorded demo plus reply-to-ask
stop_conditions: If fewer than half of contacted accounts confirm the pain, tighten must-haves
Wrong-person replies above about 1 in 5: revisit the role choice (our heuristic)
PB-cold-outreach stop rule (under 1% reply after 100 contacts)
No-show rate high: check lead time and reminders
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
Several simultaneous cold emails into one account
Long template-style emails with exclamation marks
Booking more than a week out (book: attendance falls; unquantified)

contextual_heuristic.rule: proposed: each must-have is tagged observable or not observable; non-observable traits can't be list filters and become discovery or form questions.
proposed: visible paid tiers (paid directory listing, active ads in a public ad library, a paid booking tool) count as a willingness-to-pay nice-to-have, with source URL.
proposed: follow-up steps are assigned one narrative value theme or proof each, chosen from the positioning hierarchy, so no two steps repeat a theme.
proposed: step 2 or 3 may offer a prospect-specific proof asset made from public evidence, offered without a link.
proposed: book response-rate figures (12% vs 5%, 18% at step 2) are stored as dated vendor examples, never as base rates.
proposed: booking pages offer slots within the next 7-10 days by default.
proposed: confirmed meetings get a calendar invite with agenda and a same-morning reminder email from the owner's mailbox.

strategic_preference.rule: proposed: a list uses one primary sourcing source per campaign; extra sources only enrich already-found accounts.
proposed: contact one primary role per account; add one complementary role only after the primary sequence ends without reply.
proposed: the first email carries no booking link; a booking link appears only after the prospect replies with interest.

external_requirement.rule: proposed: never source from bought or scraped contact lists without a recorded lawful basis; prospects come only from public business sources or owner-provided lists with provenance.
proposed: personal (non-business) email addresses are never a cold-email route, even when published on a profile.
proposed: subject lines starting with 'Re:' or 'Fwd:' on step 1, and any 'returning your call' wording, are lint errors.

unknown_to_investigate.rule: proposed: owner phone outreach to businesses needs a call-compliance check (UK TPS/CTPS screening, US mobile and autodialer rules) before ClimbOS suggests it.

economic_feasibility.rule: proposed: compute value per meeting = average deal value x meeting-to-win rate in code, and compare with owner hours x hourly cost before recommending meetings.

reconciliation_note: Many book tactics conflict with ClimbOS policy and are excluded (see guides/BK09_founding_sales.md).
